__baseline_prompt__.text: An SCP-inspired containment photograph of a fictional containment researcher during an interrupted anomalous-object containment test. Use the supplied reference for facial appearance and dark bob haircut: the softly tapered face, broad dark eyes, straight small nose, softly full lips, jaw-length glossy black bob and separated wispy fringe remain recognizable. Portray her as a fictional adult researcher in a pale gray laboratory jacket over a charcoal fitted knit top, with the subtle intimacy of close human attention rather than theatrical panic. In a worn concrete experimental room, she stands behind a waist-high steel workbench, her body just left of a transparent cylindrical glass hood. A small tarnished handbell hangs mouth-down inside the hood, fixed to a rigid metal support, above a shallow black dust tray. A dense, narrow stream of dark dust connects the tray to the bell mouth, climbing in a delicately curling column inside the clear air; settled dust remains scattered around the tray rim. Her left palm braces the outside steel base of the hood; her right hand wraps around the separate red-tipped locking lever mounted on the near side of that base, drawing it into its closed notch. Both forearms remain visible between her sleeves and those two distinct contacts. She leans only slightly forward, her shoulders controlled, eyes fixed on the bell and lips parted as the test changes in front of her. Beside the hood, a brass calibration weight lies tipped against the raised rim of a painted test circle, making the interrupted procedure tangible. A clipboard and capped pencil lie farther down the bench, subordinate to the bell and her hands. Compose a quiet medium-wide horizontal photograph from bench height, with her three-quarter face on the left, the glass bell enclosure on the right, and both hands across the lower central plane. One cool ceiling panel lights the room; a warm inspection lamp grazing the hood separates the dark dust against a pale background and catches a thin edge of light in her hair. The bell, dust path, lever contact and face share readable focus, with the farther concrete wall soft. Restrained steel gray, amber and black, natural skin texture, credible glass reflections, and a measured documentary stillness give one precise procedural moment the weight of an unresolved event.

__baseline_prompt__.text: Create a cinematic documentary photograph of a clinical anomalous-containment incident, with a reference-guided fictional adult woman responding to an impossible water event. Use the supplied reference for her visible facial and hair appearance: the softly tapered face, large dark eyes, straight dark chin-length bob and fine separated fringe remain recognizable. She is a fictional containment hydrologist, portrayed with composed personal presence and understated attraction in a fitted charcoal utility jumpsuit with rolled sleeves. The particular scene is a sealed hydrology vault during the last seconds of manual isolation. A shallow black pool inside the wet chamber pulls itself upward into a thick, transparent water column, visibly narrowing from its torn floor surface toward a circular stainless collector suspended above it. Separate ascending droplets have their trailing points aimed down toward the pool, while the underside of the collector receives a crown of upward splash. A dry control walkway occupies the left foreground; a thick transparent partition divides it from the wet chamber at right. On the dry side she plants both boots apart and leans forward slightly, gripping opposite sides of a red handwheel at waist height with both hands. The wheel's exposed stem joins a rigid pipe that passes through the partition and continues clearly up to the collector, making the manual response belong to this single phenomenon. Her torso, connected arms and hand contact remain visible together. She looks past the wheel toward the rising water, brows drawn and lips slightly parted with concentrated urgency. A segmented shutter across the collector mouth is halfway closed, leaving one luminous crescent still taking in water; the handwheel, pipe, shutter and column form one legible causal route. Heavy bolted seals, drain channels and a broad amber floor boundary make the chamber feel maintained and dangerous. A small observation window sits behind the anomaly, with a wall-mounted status beacon casting an amber reflection into the wet steel. Photograph from the dry walkway at the woman's chest height with a slightly wide normal lens. Keep her three-quarter face large enough to read and the entire pool-to-collector route legible in the same deep-focus frame. Cold ceiling panels establish precise wet highlights; a warmer work light grazes her cheek and forearms. The first read is her deliberate grip beside the impossible column; the sealed architecture is the quieter third layer. Preserve credible human scale, palpable humid air, and physically ordinary support for her body while the water alone behaves anomalously.

__baseline_prompt__.text: Create a fictional SCP containment photograph: a complex connected scene in which an anomalous event and a connected human response are readable together. A person with visible face and hair appearance guided by the supplied reference is portrayed as a fictional adult containment technician. Preserve the portrait's softly rounded face, large brown eyes, small nose and naturally shaped pink lips, and its jaw-length dark-brown bob with airy parted fringe. Her individuality and quiet presence carry a subtle warmth against the impersonal room. She wears a charcoal fitted work shirt beneath a light gray utility vest and practical trousers; her exposed face is three-quarter toward the camera while her eyes follow the boundary she is moving. Inside a cold-storage observation bay with pale tiled walls, a circular steel specimen ring stands upright in a transparent transport case on a low wheeled cart at the left foreground. Its size and full circular shape are clear. An empty padded cradle sits two meters behind the cart. A single inspection lamp beside that empty cradle aims directly at the rear white wall. Despite the empty cradle, an oversized crisp black ring-shaped shadow occupies the illuminated rear wall on the right, with a narrow black extension reaching down to the floor. The specimen and the detached shadow are visibly separate in the same view. The cart, empty cradle, lamp beam and wall are spaced so the contradiction can be seen at once. The technician stands in the center-right foreground on the clear side of the floor. She is rolling a hinged yellow safety barrier across the pedestrian approach to that black extension. Both hands grip the near horizontal rail shoulder-width apart; her elbows are bent, her torso inclines slightly toward the barrier, and her staggered boots remain planted on the clear floor. The barrier's caster wheels touch the floor and its far panel angles toward a wall socket, leaving a narrowing passage. Her attention follows the far end of the barrier as she closes the route. This moment shows a deliberate practical response to an impossible observation: ordinary equipment, a misplaced shadow and a human choosing where it is safe to stand. Make the visual hierarchy lead from her attentive face and connected hands to the yellow barrier, then to the black ring and its physically displaced steel counterpart. A waist-height oblique wide photograph from the room's open doorway keeps her face, hands, wheels, empty cradle, ring and wall shadow legible together. Cool overhead fluorescent illumination reveals tile seams, faint condensation at the cold door seals and brushed metal; the inspection lamp makes the anomalous silhouette crisp. Moderate depth of field, a natural 35 mm photographic perspective, restrained neutral color and believable surface wear give the scene the matter-of-fact intimacy of an incident photograph.
